newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends higher aided by weak Canada dollar.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends higher aided by weak Canada dollar.

text.p: WCE canola closed higher as a weaker Canadian dollar boosted export prospects with gains in CBOT soybeans also supportive, floor sources said.
Dealers said there was both crusher and exporter buying. Overnight sales of Canadian canola to Japan were estimated at 4,000 to 5,000 tonnes.

Flaxseed also finished higher, aided by the strength of other oilseed markets, with commission houses and locals featured buyers of old crop and commercials of new crop. March ended up $3.90 at $353.90.

Western barley prices ended higher on commercial buying with Cargill featured. The pace of hedge selling also slowed with farmers looking for higher prices following Thursday's Canadian Wheat Board Pool Return Outlook.
The CWB raised its feed barley PROs by $2.00 a tonne.
Feed wheat prices finished slightly higher in quiet conditions aided by gains in CBOT corn. March ended $0.90 higher at $169.60.
Feed peas ended higher on commercial and commission house buying with May up US$2.10 at US$198.10. Oats were tradeless.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
